news.hook: At Indian Oil’s Panipat refinery, the first batch of sustainable aviation fuel from used cooking oil has been produced, paving the way for greener flights across India.
news.name: India's First Sustainable Aviation Fuel Plant Ready at Panipat Refinery
news.summary: The plant, with a 30,000-tonne annual capacity, holds India's first ISCC CORSIA certification and all necessary approvals to meet upcoming blending mandates—1% SAF in jet fuel for international flights from 2027, rising to 5% by 2030. In parallel, Air India and Airbus signed a feasibility study on November 17 for India's first voluntary corporate SAF program, letting businesses support cleaner fuel on select routes. These steps align with India's fast-growing aviation sector, which used over 9 million tonnes of fuel in 2025-26 and eyes 14 million by 2030, while advancing Net Zero 2070 goals.
